title: Prognostic on‑call load forecaster and staggered probe executor
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Pager storms and redundant probe bursts during rotation boundaries increase noise and incident load while inflating synthetic probe cost. This PR adds two coordinated components: (1) a light-weight prognostic forecaster that predicts short-horizon oncall load (next 5–60 minutes) using stratified recent-contact rates and calendar-aware features, and (2) a staggered probe executor that schedules sampled probes across safe windows with backoff gates to avoid synchronized bursts.

What this does (single-string section): Implements a short-term forecasting service (slo-toolkit/forecaster) and a scheduling layer in the probe runner (slo-toolkit/probe/scheduler) that uses the forecast to decide probe density and staging. Key design goals: keep model computation tiny (running in-process on a single coordinator pod), deterministic fallbacks to historical percentiles if data is missing, and explicit safety gates so probes never increase error budgets or saturate oncall channels.

Checklist: 
- [x] Forecasting algorithm (exponential smoothing + light GLM ensemble) implemented and unit tested
- [x] Probe scheduler with staggered execution windows and jitter
- [x] Safety gates: max-rate cap, CPU/latency-based backoff, oncall quiet-hours override
- [x] Integration tests for coordinator + probe runner communication
- [x] Dashboard panels and alerts for forecast drift and probe throttling
- [x] Migration plan and feature flag gating for gradual rollout

Rollout plan and backward compatibility: The feature is behind feature flag slo.forecast.staggered_probes_off by default. Enable in canary namespaces first (10% traffic window), observe forecast error and throttling events for 48 hours, then increase to 50% and full rollout. If the forecaster fails or reports high error, scheduler falls back to historical median probe cadence; no consumer-facing change expected.

Telemetry and observability: New metrics exported: slo_forecast_horizon_error_{5m,15m,60m}, slo_probe_scheduled_count, slo_probe_throttled_count, slo_probe_backoff_reason (labels: cpu, latency, quiet_hours, forecast_unavailable). Added dashboard: "Oncall Forecast & Probe Scheduler" under slo-toolkit. Added tracing spans around forecasting and scheduling for end-to-end latency analysis.

Security and safety: Probes inherit RBAC and sanitization rules from existing probe runner. The scheduler includes an explicit safety circuit that prevents any increase in probe volume above a conservative cap during incidents or when SLO burn-rate alarms are firing.

Testing: Unit tests cover forecasting edge cases (sparse data, clock skew), scheduler jitter distributions, and safety gate behavior. Integration tests simulate rotation boundary spikes and validate probes are smoothed and throttled as expected. Load tests run a representative probe mix; CPU overhead observed <4% on coordinator pod at canary scale.

Related linear and context: ENG-1219 is the original spike analysis; ENG-1304 is the oncall cost reduction initiative. This PR is intentionally small-surface for easier review and rollout; follow-ups will add an optional richer LSTM model behind a flag for customers who run large fleets.

Notes: I included a short operator guide in docs/ops/oncall-forecasting.md and a migration script for older probe schedules. The next PR will add CLI toggles for per-rotation overrides.

4 commits:
- Add forecaster core (smoothing + GLM ensemble) and tests
- Implement probe scheduler with windowing and jitter
- Safety gates, metrics, and dashboard panels
- Docs and rollout/feature-flag plumbing

release_notes: Adds short-term on-call load forecasting and staggered probe scheduling to reduce probe storms and synthetic cost. Backwards compatible, feature-flagged, and ships with dashboards and alerts.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature flag slo.forecast.staggered_probes_off=false in canary namespaces to test. Watch slo_forecast_horizon_error_5m and slo_probe_throttled_count; ensure burn-rate alerts remain green during rollout. Revert by toggling flag or disabling scheduler via slo.forecast.enabled=false.
testing_summary: Unit tests: 46 new tests. Integration tests: forecast+scheduler scenario tests run in CI matrix. Load test: coordinated probe run at 2x canary scale for 30m; CPU overhead <4% on coordinator. Observed 32% reduction in probe burst peaks in synthetic validation.
additional_context: Design intentionally keeps forecasting logic lightweight and explainable so operators can reason about behavior without model op complexity. Longer-term plan: add per-customer calibration and an observational pipeline to feed cleaned features into an optional heavier model.
